answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain a personal hardware beacon that periodically signs a unique pulse incorporating the current epoch seed and prior chain hash. Peers sample these against an orchard of historical signals stored on-chain. A clone cannot forge the beacon because the private key lives in a tamper-resistant opal module bound to one physical device. An attacker wanting N identities must buy and maintain N such modules plus continuous online presence, raising cost linearly with scale.
